How this was built

  1. Each trade keeps its real fills, stop, exit and times. Profit and fees scale with the position, so the Scalper Offer's waived closing fee carries over.
  2. The record that sets leverage uses only shadow trades closed before the entry.
  3. A trade is liquidated when its recorded worst point crossed the liquidation price for its leverage; none did.
  4. Skipping a trade frees its slot, but a signal the real account refused for other reasons is not in either ledger, so the corrected books cannot take it.
  5. The shadow book is replayed as a single $1,000 account so the two can be compared; live, it still trades every signal in R and keeps its script-stop trades as evidence.
  6. The tracker's cells are left out of the shadow ledger.
